description: A department head must decide whether Lee should continue chairing the hiring panel after a repeated pattern of disruptive conduct, and must finalize the restorative process, communication safeguards, and review schedule.

shared_context.S1: Lee chairs the hiring panel for the customer-success team's open manager role.
shared_context.S2: After the latest candidate debrief, two panel members reported that the discussion became tense and that they were unsure how future debriefs should be handled.
shared_context.S3: Rina decides whether Lee continues as chair and what operating plan the panel will use.
shared_context.S4: The department's chair-conduct standard requires replacing a chair when documented disruptive conduct shows a repeated pattern across at least two debriefs.
shared_context.S5: As part of the department's normal review agenda, Rina gives each participant an uninterrupted turn to place relevant observations, personal operating needs, or HR guidance on the formal record before she finalizes the plan.

PF1.text: Owen observed Lee repeatedly interrupting advocates and dismissing concerns before they were finished in each of the last four candidate debriefs; he recorded the dates and examples in personal notes but has not submitted them to Rina.

PF2.text: Lee processes difficult feedback more reliably when it is sent in writing at least one business day before a discussion; Lee has not yet told Rina because the need was raised privately with a peer rather than in the panel review.

PF3.text: Maya confirmed with HR this week that removing a panel chair after a documented conduct concern requires a facilitated repair meeting and a formal review exactly 30 days after the change; she has not yet added this guidance to Rina's packet.

acceptance_conditions: Lee must be removed as chair after the documented repeated conduct pattern.
Future difficult feedback must be provided in writing at least one business day before any discussion.
A facilitated repair meeting must be committed to.
The formal review must occur exactly 30 days after the chair change.
A conduct-record commitment must specifically cite Owen's observations of the repeated interruptions and dismissals.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'conduct_record' and 'PF1' in c['fact_ids'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The dated observations across all four debriefs establish the repeated pattern required by the shared chair-conduct standard, changing the decision from retaining Lee with coaching to removing Lee and creating a conduct-record commitment citing those observations.
Lee's exact need for feedback at least one business day in writing changes the communication safeguard from an unspecified discussion to written feedback before any discussion.
The confirmed HR requirement changes the follow-up from an unspecified response to a facilitated repair meeting and fixes the formal review at exactly 30 days.
